solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Appeal of hit show, ultimate in chart topper?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about and thrown out of shape, so its letters get rearranged
the ultimate part of a word is its very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of chart
a topper is a top hat, or any hat worn on top

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what makes a hit show successful, perhaps its finishing position at the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: HOWS + T + HAT gives HOW'S THAT, the cry a cricket fielder or bowler makes to ask the umpire to give a batsman out. Cricket is a British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the shout asking the umpire for a dismissal is formally called an appeal, and these words are its traditional form.

clue.text: Approach plain with river

blocks.note: overt means open, plain to see
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Directions for walking across flat country beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' and 'plain' look like a walker's terrain; 'plain' is the adjective meaning obvious, and 'Approach' is a noun meaning an advance or proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Making overtures means making tentative advances or proposals to someone, so an overture is an opening approach.

clue.text: What could show small naughty child a way of seeing inside?

definitions.text: What could show small naughty child a way of seeing inside?

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an elf is a mischievous little person, used for an impish child
analysis breaks something down to look into its workings

explanation.surface: A parent wonders what might teach a badly behaved youngster to look into their own conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds the answer piece by piece, and the whole clue then describes it: examining yourself is exactly what might show an imp its own insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-analysis is introspection, the examination of one's own thoughts and motives, which is a way of looking within.

clue.text: Greeting a guard, not caught by a brave hero

indicators.note: saying a thing is not present instructs us to leave those letters out

blocks.note: a casual greeting
taken as written
to keep watch is to guard; a watch is also a guard
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the second a, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a sentry while a courageous figure looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: WATCH loses its C to become WATH, then HI + A + WATH + A. A brave here is a Native American warrior, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha is the Native American warrior who is the hero of Longfellow's narrative poem The Song of Hiawatha.

clue.text: Reading perhaps about unknown in books is of no real value

indicators.note: a thing placed about another goes around it, enclosing it
one thing set in another sits inside its walls

blocks.note: Reading is a town in Berkshire, west of London; 'perhaps' flags it as an example
Y is a mathematical unknown
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Reading matter about some anonymous subject is dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the act of reading books, but it is the Berkshire town; Y as an unknown comes from algebra, and the two containers nest one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Toytown is used as a dismissive adjective for something trivial, petty or toylike, lacking genuine substance or worth.

clue.text: Cases for neuroscience unit emergency room doctor

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell around its contents, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of neuroscience
first and last letters of unit
ER is the standard abbreviation for an emergency room

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor sees cases referred from the neuroscience unit to the emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun in a hospital scene, but it is the verb used of vets operating on animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a pet is a euphemism for castrating or spaying it, which is exactly what neutering means.

clue.text: Aircraft varnish — work into wings of drone

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside
wings sit at either side of a body, so only the two end letters are used

blocks.note: first and last letters of drone
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Varnish for an aircraft is applied to the wings of a drone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wings' look like part of the aircraft scene, but they only mean the outer letters of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is a lacquer painted onto the fabric covering of early aeroplane wings to tighten and stiffen it.

clue.text: Plays, regularly polemical, without intermission

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken
in its old sense of outside, so these letters surround another piece

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
a rest is a break or pause

explanation.surface: A critic complains that combative dramas run straight through with no interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without intermission' reads as non-stop, but 'without' means outside: the alternate letters wrap around the break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oresteia is Aeschylus's trilogy of Greek tragedies, Agamemnon, The Libation Bearers and The Eumenides.

clue.text: Accessible work — aim with old men

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an end is a goal or aim
O is the abbreviation for old
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Easy-to-understand work aimed at elderly men.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for men comes from army usage, other ranks being the private soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-door policy lets anyone come in or approach freely, so the phrase describes something readily available to all.

clue.text: Cut down fine length of cloth

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an ell is an old measure of length used for cloth

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a nice piece of fabric down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down fine' reads as cutting cloth finely; the definition is the first two words only.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it so that it falls to the ground.

clue.text: Classic tugboats reportedly out of condition?

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: something out of condition is defective
tugboats tow other vessels

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned tugs said to be in poor working order.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is the 1970s BBC sitcom starring John Cleese as a hotelier, often voted the greatest British comedy; 'Classic' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom is a celebrated British television comedy, widely regarded as a timeless masterpiece of the genre.

clue.text: Disintegrating: it’s a new maths thing

indicators.note: something disintegrating falls apart and reforms in a different order

blocks.note: the letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A complaint that some crumbling new mathematical idea is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon works as a link: the anagram signal and fodder come first and the one-word definition last.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatsitsname is a placeholder word used when the proper name of an object escapes you, much like thingummy.

clue.text: Basket turned up with new bag

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the opposite way

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: A shopper produces a basket along with a fresh carrier bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like a single phrase meaning arrived, but 'up' is the fodder and 'turned' acts on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small square container or basket in which soft fruit such as strawberries is sold in Britain.

clue.text: Ceremony upsetting Rwanda church

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them over and out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A religious service causes offence in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reads as causing distress to Rwanda, but it rearranges the country's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ritual performance by warriors before battle or in celebration, a kind of tribal rite.

clue.text: Cover telephone inventor against clash of interests

blocks.note: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone
to jar is to clash or conflict

explanation.surface: An insurance policy protects a famous inventor against conflicts of interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests insurance, with 'against' continuing that sense; it is a physical cover, and 'against' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a bell-shaped glass dome placed over delicate objects or laboratory apparatus to protect them.

clue.text: Bread with appropriate side finally covered in unlimited butter

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept
without limits means without boundaries, so the outer letters go and the middle stays
something covered in another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: to bag is to appropriate or seize
the last letter of side
butter without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A loaf served with a suitable side dish, smothered in plenty of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning seize. E goes inside UTTE after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is the long thin French loaf with a crisp crust, a familiar type of white bread.

clue.text: Running as a cure for split in foot?

indicators.note: running colours mix and lose their places, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Jogging is recommended as a remedy for a cracked or blistered foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The foot here is a metrical foot in verse, not the body part; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a caesura is a pause or break in a line of verse, which may fall within a metrical foot.

clue.text: What needs pilot broadcast on cable before start of run

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a line is a cable or wire
the opening letter of run

explanation.surface: A TV pilot episode needs airing on cable before its series run begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' and 'broadcast on cable' paint a television pilot episode; the pilot actually flies the plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aeroplane cannot fly without someone at the controls, so it is a thing requiring an aviator.

clue.text: Study due for change again

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
just as in deserved, merited, what is due

explanation.surface: A study that is overdue for another revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due for change' reads as a single phrase meaning ready to be altered; 'due' stands alone and 'for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to alter or adapt something once more, setting it differently a second time.

clue.text: Thus youth with record overturned boats

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue, so the letters run bottom to top instead

blocks.note: so means thus
a lad is a young man
an EP, extended play, is a type of record

explanation.surface: A youngster and a recording are aboard some capsized boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned boats' reads as capsized craft, but the indicator applies to the pieces before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedalos are small pleasure boats propelled by pedals, hired out at beaches and on boating lakes.

clue.text: Male succeeded when cutting to obtain a certain diamond?

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, splitting it open

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
to obtain is to get
as in 'one Mr Smith', meaning a certain person

explanation.surface: A man cuts a stone successfully to produce a particular diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests the jeweller's craft but is the container signal. 'a certain diamond' looks like the definition, but 'a certain' supplies a number, as in 'a certain Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is one kind of precious stone, so it is an example of the wider category; the question mark marks that.

clue.text: Cricketer’s heavy blow about exercise

indicators.note: a thing placed about another goes all around it

blocks.note: a oner is British slang for a hefty blow
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A batsman's mighty swing at the ball concerns his fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as a possessive but stands for 'is'. ONER wraps around PE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is one of the two batsmen who start a side's innings in cricket, a British bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Religious song but not second pious ceremonial

indicators.note: excluding something removes it, leaving the remainder

blocks.note: a spiritual is an African-American religious folk song
S is the abbreviation for second
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A hymn that is ceremonial but not very devout.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIRITUAL loses S and PI from its front to leave the answer; 'pious' looks like part of the definition but is a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual as an adjective describes acts performed according to a fixed solemn form, the same as formal or ceremonial.

clue.text: Drawing on veracities in a new way

indicators.note: doing something in a new way means arranging it differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist draws upon truths, reinterpreting them freshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing on' reads as using a source; 'on' belongs to the fodder and 'Drawing' is the gruesome old sense, as in hanged, drawn and quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a carcass or a condemned prisoner was to remove the entrails, which is disembowelling.

clue.text: Climbing team traps live mountain goat

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
trapping something holds it captive within

blocks.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a football or cricket team
to be is to live, to exist

explanation.surface: A mountaineering party catches a live wild goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing team' paints mountaineers, apt for the goat; it really says to flip the team, then trap the verb inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of Alpine and other high mountain regions, known for its long curved horns.

clue.text: Queen wearing gold and a pale blue

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in gold and a light blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is wearing the gold, so Q sits inside AU, and A is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a light greenish-blue colour named after the Latin word for water.

clue.text: Book lasting a year?

blocks.note: surface reading: a volume that takes, or covers, a whole year
setter's reading: a year is a dozen months, and the abbreviation for months is mo, so the book-size term splits as a span of time

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TWELVE MO and it reads as twelve months; joined, it is a printer's term for a page size, also written 12mo.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemo, or duodecimo, is a small book size made by folding each printed sheet into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Italian town, no resort for development

indicators.note: land earmarked for development will be rebuilt into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian town not yet a holiday resort is earmarked for building work.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironically Sorrento is a famous resort, so the surface claim is false as well as cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a coastal town on the Bay of Naples in southern Italy, overlooking the island of Capri.
